Saint Bartholomew is one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus, who is believed to have preached the Gospel in various regions of the Middle East, Armenia, and even India. The feast day of Saint Bartholomew, August 24, is celebrated with much fervor, particularly in the Iberian Peninsula. The cult of Saint Bartholomew has also produced numerous works of art and literature, further cementing his place in Western spiritual and cultural history.

Moreover, the name Bartolome bring to mind the suffering and martyrdom of Saint Bartholomew, who is believed to have been flayed alive. Thus, the name represents a call to bear witness to our beliefs, even in the face of adversity and persecution.
